title: Toddler who will not stop fitting
description: A mother carries in her 2-year-old son, who has been fitting for about 10 minutes and has a fever.

speaker.name: Palesa Mahlangu
speaker.style: Very distressed and crying. She calms a little when someone takes charge.

presenting_complaint: Jerking of all four limbs for about 10 minutes, with a fever and a cough since yesterday.
opening_line: Sister, he is shaking and won't wake up! It started at home, it is not stopping!
personality: Overwhelmed; she answers best when questions are short.

history.onset: The jerking started at home about 10 minutes ago and has not stopped.
history.fever: He has had a fever and a cough since yesterday; she gave paracetamol syrup this morning.
history.previous_seizures: He had one short fit with a fever last year that stopped by itself.
history.ingestion: No tablets or chemicals at home that he could have taken.
history.rash_and_neck: She has not noticed a rash.

disclosure.label: How long the seizure has lasted

ground_truth.diagnosis: Convulsive status epilepticus with fever in a toddler
expected_actions: time the seizure; protect the airway, place in the recovery position, suction and give high-flow oxygen
check the blood glucose; if below 3 mmol/L give 10 percent dextrose 2 millilitres per kilogram

give a benzodiazepine: buccal or intranasal midazolam 0.3 milligrams per kilogram (about 4 milligrams for 13 kilograms; maximum 10 milligrams), or intravenous lorazepam 0.1 milligrams per kilogram, or rectal diazepam 0.5 milligrams per kilogram
repeat the benzodiazepine once after 5 to 10 minutes if still fitting
second line if still fitting: levetiracetam 40 to 60 milligrams per kilogram intravenously, or phenytoin 20 milligrams per kilogram over 20 minutes with monitoring
call for help and arrange urgent transfer; treat the fever and look for meningitis

vitals.result: Weight 13 kg. Generalised jerking, eyes rolled up, saliva in the mouth. No rash seen.

aspirin.warning: Aspirin is not given to children for this problem; it risks Reye syndrome and bleeding.

iv_access.result: Cannula sited at the second attempt; bloods taken.

call_ambulance.result: Ambulance requested urgently. Estimated arrival 20 minutes.

escalate_doctor.result: Doctor informed using SBAR and on the way.

hints: How long has he been fitting? Protect him and his airway first.
Give oxygen and check the glucose.
After 5 minutes of fitting a first-line drug is due; work out the dose from his weight.
If he is still fitting 5 to 10 minutes later, plan the next step and call for help.

ideal_approach: Time the seizure; airway, recovery position, suction and high-flow oxygen.
Check glucose; 10 percent dextrose 2 millilitres per kilogram if below 3 mmol/L.
Buccal or intranasal midazolam 0.3 milligrams per kilogram (about 4 milligrams for 13 kilograms), repeat once after 5 to 10 minutes.
Second line: levetiracetam 40 to 60 milligrams per kilogram or phenytoin 20 milligrams per kilogram over 20 minutes.
Call for help and transfer; treat the fever and consider meningitis.
debrief.model_answer: Neo is 30 months old and 13 kg, fitting for more than 10 minutes with a fever of 39.4 and a saturation of 88 percent: convulsive status epilepticus. Protect the airway, place him on his side, suction and give high-flow oxygen. Check the glucose (4.9 mmol/L, normal). Give buccal midazolam 0.3 milligrams per kilogram (about 4 milligrams) now and repeat once after 5 to 10 minutes if he is still fitting; then levetiracetam 40 to 60 milligrams per kilogram or phenytoin 20 milligrams per kilogram. Call for help and an ambulance, treat the fever and look for meningitis.
reflection_questions: Why does a seizure longer than 5 minutes need treatment?
How did you calculate the midazolam dose?
What would make you think of meningitis?
references: National Department of Health. Standard Treatment Guidelines and Essential Medicines List for South Africa: Paediatric Hospital Level. Latest edition.
Advanced Paediatric Life Support (APLS): The Practical Approach. Latest edition.
World Health Organization. Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children. 2nd edition.
debrief.review_note: Draft paediatric case written for the app. Doses and steps follow common paediatric emergency practice and need clinician review against the current South African guidelines before teaching use.

learning_objectives: Manage the airway in a fitting child
Give first- and second-line anticonvulsants by weight
